modern: “The earth loves the shower”; and “the solemn ether loves”; and the universe loves to make whatever is about to be. I say then to the universe that I love as you love. And is this not also what is meant by saying that “this or that loves,” that is, tends, “to be produced”?

explained.summary:
Marcus borrows lines of poetry about the earth loving the rain and the sky loving to send it, and applies them to the universe, which loves to bring about whatever comes next. His reply is simple: then I love what you love.

He also plays on a Greek turn of phrase in which ’it loves to happen’ just means ’it tends to happen’. Accepting events becomes something warmer than resignation, a kind of agreement with the way things unfold.
